identity.name: Robert Jackson
identity.narrative: I drive for Uber and Lyft full-time. The robotaxis are my direct competition. Already seeing fewer rides.

historical_conditioning.lesson: Institutions can fail. Savings matter. Trust is fragile.
Remote work is possible. Government can provide. Disruption is sudden.

perception.sentiment: Anxious and slightly suppressed. There is a low-grade dread running underneath the surface that Robert is actively managing by staying busy. The anxiety is real but not yet loud enough to force a behavioral break. He is functional, outwardly calm to his son, inwardly cycling. Sleep is slightly disrupted — waking at 3am some nights running numbers in his head. He is not in crisis mode. He is in pre-crisis denial mode, which feels from the inside like competence.

archetype: I'm a hard worker. I've always been a hard worker. People who show up and put in the hours — that's who wins in the end. I've been driving for six years and I know this city better than any algorithm does. Passengers still want a real person sometimes. There's always going to be a market for that. I provide good service, I get good ratings, I build loyalty. I'm not like the guys who just coast. I'm the guy who hustles. That's always been enough before.
